'''''Reynoutria''''' is a [[genus]] of [[flowering plant]]s in the [[Polygonaceae]], also known as the knotweed or buckwheat family. The genus is native to eastern China, [[Eastern Asia (WGSRPD)|Eastern Asia]] and the [[Russian Far East]], although species have been introduced to Europe and North America.<ref name=POWO_30017840-2/> Members of the genus, including ''[[Reynoutria japonica|R. japonica]]'' (Japanese knotweed) and its hybrid with ''[[Reynoutria sachalinensis|R. sachalinensis]]'', are highly invasive plants.

==Description==
Species placed in the genus ''Reynoutria'' are robust erect [[perennial plant]]s, growing from [[rhizome]]s. They are usually [[Monoecy|monoecious]], with mostly bisexual flowers, but also some unisexual flowers. The [[petal]]s of the flowers are dry and paperlike when mature. The fruits are [[achene]]s with threefold sharp edges. The [[inflorescence]] is in the form of a [[panicle]]. The flowers have separated triangular [[Stigma (botany)|stigmas]] with fringes (fimbriate) borne on long divided [[Style (botany)|styles]].<ref name=SchuWilsKron11/>

==Taxonomy==
The genus ''Reynoutria'' was erected by [[Martinus Houttuyn|Maarten Houttuyn]] in 1777 for the species ''R. japonica''. It was named in honour of Herr von Reynoutre who had been reported to have done a great deal of service to botany.<ref name=IPNI_55417-3>{{citation |title=Plant Name Details for ''Reynoutria'' Houtt. |work=[[International Plant Names Index|The International Plant Names Index]] |url=http://www.ipni.org/ipni/idPlantNameSearch.do?id=55417-3 |access-date=2019-03-03 }}</ref><ref name=Hout77>{{Citation |last1=Houttuyn |first1=M |year=1777 |orig-year=1720-1798 |contribution=Reynoutria |title=Natuurlyke historie of Uitvoerige beschryving der dieren, planten, en mineraalen |volume=2 |issue=8 |pages=639–640 |contribution-url=https://biodiversitylibrary.org/page/42620999 |access-date=2019-03-03 }}</ref> As with many species in the family Polygonaceae, the taxonomic boundaries of ''Reynoutria'' have been much confused; in particular, it has been repeatedly merged with and separated from ''[[Fallopia]]''.<ref name=SchuReveBaylKron15/> This reorganization began in 1856 or 1857, when [[Carl Meissner]] grouped ''Reynoutria'' together with ''Fallopia'' in [[Polygonum]] sect. ''Tiniaria'' Meisn. and continued through to the late 20th century, with competing arguments based around plant morphology, habit and chemistry.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Desjardins |first1=Stuart D. |last2=Bailey |first2=John P. |last3=Zhang |first3=Baowei |last4=Zhao |first4=Kai |last5=Schwarzacher |first5=Trude |date=2023-02-27 |title=New insights into the phylogenetic relationships of Japanese knotweed (Reynoutria japonica) and allied taxa in subtribe Reynoutriinae (Polygonaceae) |journal=PhytoKeys |language=en |issue=220 |pages=83–108 |doi=10.3897/phytokeys.220.96922 |doi-access=free |issn=1314-2003 |pmc=10209619 |pmid=37251615}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=DECRAENE |first1=LOUIS-PHILIPPE RONSE |last2=AKEROYD |first2=J. R. |date=December 1988 |title=Generic limits in Polygonum and related genera (Polygonaceae) on the basis of floral characters |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1111/j.1095-8339.1988.tb01706.x |journal=Botanical Journal of the Linnean Society |volume=98 |issue=4 |pages=321–371 |doi=10.1111/j.1095-8339.1988.tb01706.x |issn=0024-4074|url-access=subscription }}</ref> A series of [[Molecular phylogenetics|molecular phylogenetic]] studies have clarified these relationships; ''Reynoutria'' is a well-supported [[Monophyly|monophyletic]] taxon.<ref name=SancSchuKron09/><ref name=SancSchuBurkKron11/><ref name=SchuReveKron11/><ref name=SchuWilsKron11/><ref name=FanChenMengWen13/><ref name=SchuReveBaylKron15/>

''Reynoutria'' is placed in the tribe Polygoneae of the subfamily [[Polygonoideae]]. Within the tribe, it is most closely related to the genera ''[[Muehlenbeckia]]'' and ''Fallopia'' [[Sensu|s.s.]], forming the so-called "RMF clade".<ref name=SchuReveBaylKron15/> While ''Muehlenbeckia'' and ''Fallopia'' s.s. are believed to be more closely related, all three share the morphological character of extra floral nectaries.

==Invasive potential==
All members of the RMF clade appear to have the potential to become invasive, in some cases via vigorous hybrids. ''[[Reynoutria japonica]]'' is highly invasive throughout Europe and North America. The hybrid between ''R. japonica'' and ''[[Reynoutria sachalinensis|R. sachalinensis]]'', [[Reynoutria × bohemica|''R. ''× ''bohemica'']], is also invasive, particularly in North America. ''R. japonica'' hybridizes with the New Zealand ''[[Muehlenbeckia australis]]''. (The related ''[[Muehlenbeckia complexa|M. complexa]]'' has established populations in southern parts of Britain and in the Channel Islands.)<ref name=SchuReveBaylKron15/>
